the analysis of the spectral properties of the standard model of nonrelativistic QED, a model for atoms and molecules in which electrons are coupled to the quantised radiation field.

the standard model of nonrelativistic QED is stable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the standard model of nonrelativistic QED can be treated as a nonrelativistic quantum field theory in the same spirit as the Nelson model.
the ground state energy can be treated as an eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian, while the excited energy spectrum is absolutely continuous.
we have shown that the second quantized dilatation operator is a good conjugate operator for the standard model of nonrelativistic QED in a neighborhood of zero energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the second quantized dilatation generator is a useful tool in spectral analysis of non-relativstic QED.
this operator can be used to control the dynamics of the standard model of nonrelativistic QED even when the electrons are non-relativistic.
this conjugate operator can be used to prove a Mourre-type estimate and a limiting absorbtion principle for a large class of non-relativstic models of QED.
